Vanessa / Marcus —

Quick background: MedCore (Lucy Huang, Head of Platform) just finished a pilot and asked for an unusual concession while they move to a 12-month committed plan. They’re proposing: 30% off list Hosted API usage price for a 12‑month term in exchange for a 3M token/month committed baseline and a 12‑month prepay of 6 months up front.

Why they ask: 1) They want predictable unit economics for an embedded feature rollout in Q3, 2) They plan to expand to two additional regions in H2 (multi-region capacity will be important), and 3) they’re willing to be a case study/partner on our marketplace.

Impact: at our current list this is a ~30% ARR margin hit in year one relative to typical net pricing for similar volumes. Ben attached the usage model and their draft SOW (MedCore_Monthly_Usage_Model.xlsx, MedCore_SOW_redline_v2.pdf).

Request: Can Deal Desk / Finance confirm whether we can grant 30% or whether we should hold to 20% (which is Dealmaker/auto-approve limit)? If >20% needs exec signoff, please advise next steps and who we should loop. We’re targeting to close and get the contract signed (DocuSign link below) by 2027-04-08 to align with their engineering ramp.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/contacts/MC-2027-042
DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/en/partners/medcore/MC-2027-042

Ben

Vanessa / team —

I ran a preliminary P&L for the ask. Short summary: at 30% off list for the proposed committed baseline (3M tokens/mo) across 12 months, net contribution margin drops to ~18% in year one after expected infra and support uplift for multi-region traffic. With the 6-month prepay that improves cash runway but doesn't change unit economics.

Options:
- Approve 25% max today with a clause to reevaluate at month 6 against usage and retention metrics (this keeps margin ~23%).
- If leadership wants 30%, I need explicit CRO/CEO signoff because the concession exceeds standard finance-authorized thresholds and creates precedent. If execs approve, we should include: a) a minimum committed spend clause, b) a 6‑month prepaid milestone, c) a quarterly usage review, and d) right to revert pricing on overages.

I’ve attached a short pricing summary image (pricing_summary.png) and a backup calc.

Questions for Ben / Vanessa before we escalate:
1) Is MedCore able to confirm the 6-month prepay today?
2) Is there a legal or data residency requirement for the multi-region expansion that adds cost?
3) Are they signing the SOW as-is or proposing any additional SLAs?

If you confirm the prepay + limited SLAs, I’ll draft the memo for Mina’s review to take to exec clear.

—Marcus

Attachments: pricing_summary.png (summary chart)

Thanks Marcus — and thanks team for the clear summary.

Business rationale checks out: MedCore is strategic (marketplace signal + multi-region expansion) and 3M tokens/month committed once ramped materially changes the LTV math. I’m comfortable recommending the 30% concession for a 12‑month term provided we put firm guardrails in place:
1) 6‑month prepay required and non-refundable toward the year commitment,
2) Minimum committed spend clause (3M tokens/month floor),
3) Quarterly usage & ROI checkpoint with right to revert pricing if usage falls below 60% of commitment for two consecutive quarters,
4) Legal to sign off on the SOW redlines (no expanded SLA beyond our standard enterprise terms).

That said, because our documented threshold for automated approval is 20%, this is an executive-level sanction. Marcus please route the short memo to Finance + Legal and mark for my final sanction. If Finance and Legal sign off on the guardrails above, I will sign the approval for 30% and authorize Deal Desk to execute the DocuSign envelope.

I want the packet (memo + financials + SOW redline) in my inbox by EOD tomorrow so I can sign before their target 4/8 close.
